newsitem.title: CANADA: NorTel shares tumble on software woes.
newsitem.headline: NorTel shares tumble on software woes.

text.p: Northern Telecom Ltd shares tumbled on Wednesday as investors grew concerned about software problems with the roll-out of its equipment on the Sprint personal communications services (PCS) network.
"The company's facing some delays on their CDMA product for the Sprint Spectrum," said Nikos Theodosopoulos of UBS Securities.
"There are some software issues with the CDMA equipment. It doesn't appear to be an issue relating to the radio technology -- it's network monitoring and maintenance," he added.
NorTel is expected to resolve this issue by mid- to late January but it will push back the roll-out of the Sprint system in those markets to be supplied by NorTel.
NorTel shares shed 4.70 to 84.40 in relatively heavy trade in Toronto. In New York, they fell 1-7/8 to 62-1/2.
Company officials were not available for comment.

Theodosopoulos expects NorTel to recognize roughly US$200 million to US$250 million in the fourth quarter of this year. He said given the delay, between US$50 million and US$100 million of these may slip into the first quarter of 1997 from the fourth quarter.

But NorTel has 30 to 60 days to resolve the problem before it has to pay any "meaningful" penalties to Sprint and may therefore recognize all the revenue this quarter, Theodosopoulos. He is maintaining all his earnings estimates for the company and his buy rating because this is only a minor delay in a major new technology.
"Obviously the concern is will they fix it in the timeframe (allowed)," he said.
((Sarah Edmonds, Reuters Toronto Bureau (416) 941-8100, E-mail sarah.edmonds@reuters.com))
